Flags that are only red and white.Japan: The Hinomaru is red disc on white. Its design is so simple that it was made the official flag only in 1999, though it was used for centuries before.
Flags that are only red and white.Canada: The red maple leaf sits between two red bars. Its colors were declared national colors by King George V in 1921.
Flags that are only red and white.Switzerland: One of two square national flags, and its white cross on red is famed for the Red Cross symbol, which reverses the colors.
Flags that are only red and white.Denmark: Its white Nordic cross on red is called the Dannebrog and is the world's oldest national flag still in use.
Flags that are only red and white.Poland: White over red is a simple pair. The flag is unusual because it's the reverse of Indonesia's, which is red over white.
Flags that are only red and white.Austria: Red, white, red bands and little else. Legend says Duke Leopold V's white tunic was stained with blood but for a belt, at the siege of Acre.
Flags that are only red and white.Indonesia: Red over white. It's almost identical to Monaco's, and the difference is a tiny proportion change.
Flags that are only red and white.Monaco: It's red over white and nearly identical to Indonesia's. Monaco's is slightly more square, and the colors come from the Grimaldi family arms.
Flags that are only red and white.Bahrain: A white band at the hoist is separated from red by a serrated edge of five triangles, standing for the five pillars of Islam.
Flags that are only red and white.Tunisia: Red with a white disc holding a red crescent and star. It's only red and white, even though the central symbol is complex.
Flags that are only red and white.Turkey: A red field with a white crescent and star. It fits because there's no other color, and it's reportedly one of the oldest national flag designs.
Flags that are only red and white.Singapore: Red over white, with a crescent and five stars in the corner. The whole design uses just those two colors, which stand for universal brotherhood and purity.
Flags that are only red and white.Georgia: A white field with a large red St. George's cross and four smaller crosses, the Five Cross Flag, restored in 2004 after the Rose Revolution.
Flags that are only red and white.Lebanon: Red and white stripes are joined by a green cedar tree, so it's not purely red and white. The cedar is a national symbol.
Flags that are only red and white.China: A red field with five yellow stars, so yellow breaks the pair. Red stands for revolution.
Flags that are only red and white.Vietnam: The red flag with a yellow star isn't just red and white, because of the star.
Flags that are only red and white.USA: Red, white and blue. The blue canton with stars spoils the red and white pair.
Flags that are only red and white.UK: The Union Flag adds blue to red and white, and the blue field is what stops it from qualifying.
Flags that are only red and white.Norway: A red flag with a blue cross fringed in white. The blue means it isn't only red and white.
Flags that are only red and white.Czech Republic: Its white and red bands are joined by a blue triangle at the hoist, added to set the flag apart from Poland's. So it isn't just red and white.
Flags that are only red and white.Albania: A red field with a black double-headed eagle. The black spoils the red and white idea, though the eagle is the country's emblem.
Flags that are only red and white.Chile: Its white and red stripes share the flag with a blue square holding a white star, so blue breaks the pair.
Flags that are only red and white.Morocco: A red flag with a green star, the Seal of Solomon. The green means it isn't red and white.
Flags that are only red and white.Iceland: Blue with a white-edged red cross, so it uses three colors, even though its design looks like Norway's.

Things you'll find in Australia.Uluru: The giant red sandstone monolith, sacred to the Anangu people, extends deep underground and is about 348 metres high; climbing it was banned in 2019.
Things you'll find in Australia.Great Barrier Reef: The largest coral structure on Earth stretches over 2,000 kilometres and is visible from space, though parts have been hit by bleaching.
Things you'll find in Australia.Sydney Opera House: Its sail-like roof is tiled with over a million Swedish ceramic tiles, and it was designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon, who left before it opened.
Things you'll find in Australia.Bondi Beach: This Sydney beach's name comes from an Aboriginal word for waves breaking over rocks, and it hosts the world's oldest surf lifesaving clubs.
Things you'll find in Australia.Kangaroo Island: Australia's third-largest island is a wildlife haven, with sea lions, koalas, and kangaroos found roaming free.
Things you'll find in Australia.Tasmania: The island state's remote forests hold some of the planet's tallest flowering trees, and the endangered Tasmanian devil.
Things you'll find in Australia.Outback: The vast, dry interior covering most of the continent is sparsely populated, with some cattle stations larger than entire countries.
Things you'll find in Australia.Great Ocean Road: Built by returned soldiers after World War I as a memorial, this Victorian coastal route passes the Twelve Apostles rock stacks.
Things you'll find in Australia.Kakadu: Australia's largest national park has rock art tens of thousands of years old, and it is a UNESCO site for both nature and culture.
Things you'll find in Australia.Daintree: This Queensland rainforest is about 180 million years old, thought to be among the oldest on Earth, and it meets the Great Barrier Reef.
Things you'll find in Australia.Whitsundays: A group of about 74 islands off Queensland, including Whitehaven Beach with its famously pure white silica sand.
Things you'll find in Australia.Harbour Bridge: Sydney's steel arch, opened in 1932, is nicknamed the Coathanger, and visitors can climb to its top.
Things you'll find in Australia.Milford Sound: A New Zealand fjord, not Australian, that Rudyard Kipling called the eighth wonder of the world, in the South Island's Fiordland.
Things you'll find in Australia.Rotorua: A New Zealand city on the North Island known for bubbling geothermal mud pools, geysers and rich Māori culture.
Things you'll find in Australia.Hobbiton: The movie set in New Zealand's Waikato region was built for Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings and Hobbit films.
Things you'll find in Australia.Bay of Islands: A subtropical New Zealand area with 144 islands, and the site of the 1840 Treaty of Waitangi signing.
Things you'll find in Australia.Queenstown: The self-styled adventure capital of New Zealand, where commercial bungee jumping began in 1988 at the Kawarau Bridge.
Things you'll find in Australia.Fiji: A South Pacific nation of more than 300 islands, separate from Australia, famous for coral reefs and kava ceremonies.
Things you'll find in Australia.Bali: An Indonesian island, with Hindu temples, in a mostly Muslim country, and a popular getaway for many Australians.
Things you'll find in Australia.Ha Long Bay: A Vietnamese bay dotted with nearly 2,000 limestone islands, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site far from Australia.
Things you'll find in Australia.Table Mountain: The flat-topped landmark above Cape Town, South Africa, sometimes covered by a cloud called the tablecloth.
Things you'll find in Australia.Fox Glacier: A New Zealand glacier on the South Island that descends unusually low, almost into temperate rainforest.
Things you'll find in Australia.Franz Josef Glacier: A New Zealand glacier named after an Austrian emperor, famed for flowing nearly down to rainforest near sea level.
Things you'll find in Australia.Mount Cook: New Zealand's tallest peak at about 3,724 metres, called Aoraki by the Māori, and it's where Edmund Hillary trained.

Canyons and gorges.Three Gorges: This stretch of the Yangtze is dammed by the Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest power station by capacity.
Canyons and gorges.Waimea Canyon: Hawaii's Waimea Canyon on Kauai is nicknamed the Grand Canyon of the Pacific, with red cliffs and waterfalls.
Canyons and gorges.Blyde River Canyon: South Africa's Blyde River Canyon is one of the biggest green canyons, and 'Blyde' means 'joyful' in Afrikaans.
Canyons and gorges.Tara Canyon: The Tara Canyon in Montenegro is among Europe's deepest, up to about 1,300 meters, and a popular rafting route.
Canyons and gorges.Samaria Gorge: Crete's Samaria Gorge is one of Europe's longest gorges, a roughly 16 km hike through a national park.
Canyons and gorges.Monument Valley: Monument Valley is a field of towering sandstone buttes rather than a canyon, and a famous backdrop of John Ford's westerns.
Canyons and gorges.Uluru: Uluru is a giant sandstone monolith in the Australian outback, sacred to the Anangu, and it rises, not drops.
Canyons and gorges.Half Dome: Half Dome is a granite dome in Yosemite, a rock face rather than a canyon.
Canyons and gorges.Old Faithful: Old Faithful is a Yellowstone geyser that erupts about every 90 minutes, a spout rather than a gorge.
Canyons and gorges.Kilimanjaro: Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest mountain, a volcano, so it's the opposite of a canyon.
Canyons and gorges.Mount Fuji: Mount Fuji is Japan's iconic volcano, a peak, not a gorge.
Canyons and gorges.Dead Sea: The Dead Sea is a salt lake whose shore is the lowest dry land on Earth, not a canyon.
Canyons and gorges.Ha Long Bay: Ha Long Bay in Vietnam is a bay dotted with thousands of limestone islands, not a canyon.
Canyons and gorges.Matterhorn: The Matterhorn is a pyramid-shaped Alpine peak, so it rises rather than cuts down.
Canyons and gorges.Great Barrier Reef: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure, visible from space, but it is a reef, not a gorge.
Canyons and gorges.Table Mountain: Table Mountain, flat-topped above Cape Town, is a mountain, not a canyon.
Canyons and gorges.Mount Etna: Mount Etna in Sicily is among the world's most active volcanoes, a mountain rather than a gorge.

Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Neil Armstrong: On July 20, 1969 he became the first human on the Moon, and he took far more of the photos than appear with him in them.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Buzz Aldrin: The second person on the Moon, he later described the lunar landscape with the phrase magnificent desolation.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Pete Conrad: Commander of Apollo 12 in 1969, he made the second landing, and he was famously the shortest of the lunar crew.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Alan Shepard: Commander of Apollo 14, he was America's first man in space, and on the Moon he hit two golf balls with a makeshift club.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Edgar Mitchell: The Apollo 14 lunar module pilot who conducted a famously unofficial ESP experiment from space and later founded the Institute of Noetic Sciences.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.David Scott: Commander of Apollo 15 and the first to drive the lunar rover, he also dropped a hammer and a feather to show they fall together.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.James Irwin: The Apollo 15 lunar module pilot who later became an evangelist and led expeditions searching for Noah's Ark on Mount Ararat.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.John Young: Commander of Apollo 16 and a veteran who flew in Gemini and later the first space shuttle flight, Columbia in 1981.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Charles Duke: At 36, the youngest person to walk on the Moon, he did it on Apollo 16 and left a family photo on the surface.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Eugene Cernan: The last person to walk on the Moon, in December 1972 on Apollo 17, and no one has stood there since.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Harrison Schmitt: A geologist and the only scientist among the Moonwalkers, he flew on Apollo 17, and he later served as a US senator.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Michael Collins: He flew around the Moon on Apollo 11 and stayed in orbit while Armstrong and Aldrin landed, so he never walked on it.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Yuri Gagarin: The first human in space in 1961, he orbited Earth once and never traveled to the Moon.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.John Glenn: The first American to orbit Earth in 1962, he later became a senator and flew again at 77, but never reached the Moon.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Jim Lovell: He commanded Apollo 13, which never landed after an oxygen tank exploded, and he flew to the Moon twice without landing.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Jack Swigert: He was a late stand-in on Apollo 13 after Ken Mattingly was exposed to measles, then helped save the crew when an oxygen tank exploded.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Fred Haise: The Apollo 13 lunar module pilot whose planned Moon landing was cancelled when an oxygen tank exploded; the crew returned safely around the Moon.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Sally Ride: In 1983 she became the first American woman in space, and no woman has yet walked on the Moon.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Valentina Tereshkova: The first woman in space in 1963 aboard Vostok 6, she orbited Earth 48 times.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Alexei Leonov: In 1965 he made the first spacewalk, from Voskhod 2, and he was a skilled artist who sketched in orbit.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Gus Grissom: A Mercury and Gemini astronaut who died in the Apollo 1 fire in 1967, before any lunar mission flew.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Chris Hadfield: A Canadian astronaut who sang a cover of Space Oddity on the ISS, but he's never visited the Moon.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Scott Kelly: He spent nearly a year aboard the ISS in 2015 to 2016, but no one has returned to the Moon since 1972.
Astronauts who walked on the Moon.Frank Borman: He commanded Apollo 8, the first crewed flight around the Moon in 1968, but he did not land.
